questions.stem: A man presents with a mixed infection of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum in a health centre in Rajasthan. What is the dosage of the treatment given on the second day?

options.label: A
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

options.label: B
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 7.5mg

options.label: C
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg 49.05% + Sulphadoxine 1500mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

options.label: D
options.text: 4 tablets of Artesunate 45mg + Sulphadoxine 1500mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 7.5mg

questions.answerText: 4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg
questions.solutionHtml:
4 tablets of Artesunate 50mg + 6 tablets of Primaquine 2.5mg

Mixed P. falciparum and P. vivax infection:

  • This is to be treated as falciparum malaria with ACT other than artesunate + sulfa-pyrimethamine, because sulfa-pyrimethamine is not effective against P. vivax. Anti relapse treatment with a 14-day course of primaquine may be started concurrently.
  • Artesunate plus Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine is given on 1st day, and from 2nd day artesunate plus primaquine.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 877-878

questions.stem: Which of the following beta-adrenergic blockers are beneficial for patients with reduced ejection fraction and can reduce mortality in chronic heart failure without causing exacerbations over a few years?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bisoprolol
  • Beta blocker approved for chronic CHF are metoprolol, bisoprolol and carvedilol. Hence, option D is correct.
  • Introduced gradually and maintained for long term, these drugs retard the progression of CHF and prolong life.
  • The benefit may result from antagonism of deleterious effects of sympathetic overactivity (invoked reflexly by heart failure) on the myocardium.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 164-165

questions.stem: A 75-year-old female presented with urinary incontinence. She also has cognitive decline and dementia. Which of the following drugs is useful for treating urinary incontinence?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tolterodine
  • Tolterodine is a M3 selective muscarinic antagonist that has preferential action on urinary bladder; It is indicated in overactive bladder with urinary frequency and urgency.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 129

questions.stem: Which drug is used to treat multiple myeloma that is known to cause reactivation of Herpes Zoster?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bortezomib
  • Bortezomib is a first-generation inhibitor of proteasome-mediated protein degradation that has a central role in the treatment of MM.
  • It has immunosuppressant properties and can reactivate herpes zoster virus.
  • Patients should receive antiviral prophylaxis if they are receiving therapy with bortezomib.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1227

questions.stem: A patient presented with breathing difficulty and nasal polyposis when he took aspirin for fever. He faced this issue previously too when he took aspirin. Which among the following is not true about this?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no allergic sensitization to aspirin and its metabolites

options.label: C
options.text: Occur on exposure to only aspirin

options.label: D
options.text: Occurs with exposure to other NSAIDs too that block COX 1

questions.answerText: Occur on exposure to only aspirin
questions.solutionHtml:
Occur on exposure to only aspirin
  • Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), also known as Samter’s Triad, is a chronic medical condition that consists of three clinical features: asthma, sinus disease with recurrent nasal polyps, and sensitivity to aspirin and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that inhibit an enzyme called cyclooxygenase-1.
  • The characteristic feature of AERD is that patients develop reactions to aspirin and other NSAIDs. Hence, option C is incorrect.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 214-215

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy presents with a two-week history of persistent fever, fatigue, and pallor. His parents also report easy bruising and gum bleeding. On examination, he is pale with petechiae on his legs, hepatosplenomegaly, and generalized lymphadenopathy. Blood tests show severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated white blood cell count with blast cells. What is the most appropriate initial treatment regimen for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisolone + Vincristine
  • This clinical symptom is suggestive of childhood leukemia.
  • Vincristine with glucocorticoids is the treatment of choice to induce remissions in patients with childhood leukemia and in combination with alkylating agents and anthracycline for those with pediatric sarcomas.
  • Vincristine is tolerated better by children than by adults, who may experience severe, progressive neurological toxicity and require lowering of the dose


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1187

questions.stem: A hypertensive patient with chronic kidney disease was having frequent attacks of renal colic. Which of the following diuretics is used?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hydrochlorothiazide
  • Hydrochlorothiazide is used in Hypercalciuria with recurrent calcium stones in the kidney. Thiazides act by reducing Ca2+ excretion. Hence, option C is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 630-631

questions.stemHtml: Identify the drug marked as 'X' in the image:tPA - Tissue Plasminogen Activator
questions.solutionHtml:
Amino caproic acid

● X drug is Amino caproic acid. ε-Aminocaproic acid and tranexamic acid are lysine analogues that compete for lysine binding sites on plasminogen and plasmin, thereby blocking their interaction with fibrin.

● Therefore, these agents inhibit fibrinolysis and can reverse states that are associated with excessive fibrinolysis.



Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 596

questions.stem: Which drug is used for maintenance therapy in opium addiction?
questions.solutionHtml:
Buprenorphine
  • Buprenorphine, a partial agonist at the MOR, represents a major change in the treatment of opiate addiction.
  • This drug produces minimal withdrawal symptoms when discontinued and has a low potential for overdose, a long duration of action, and the ability to block heroin effects, hence used for maintenance therapy in opium addiction.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 439

questions.stem: A patient who recently underwent surgery has complaints of nausea and vomiting. He was prescribed a drug called aprepitant. What is its mechanism of action?
questions.solutionHtml:
NK-1 antagonist
  • Aprepitant is a selective, high affinity NK1 receptor antagonist that blocks the emetic action of substance P, with little effect on 5 HT3 and D2 or other receptors.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 718

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman diagnosed with diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome presented to the casualty with severe abdominal pain. She was prescribed a drug that exerts a direct spasmolytic effect on the smooth muscles of the gastrointestinal tract. Which drug could it be?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dicyclomine
  • Dicyclomine has direct smooth muscle relaxant action in addition to weak and somewhat M1 selective anticholinergic action. It exerts antispasmodic action at doses which produce few atropinic side effects. Hence, option A is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition Page No. 129

questions.stem: A patient is started on a 3 HP TPT regimen. Which of the following is true regarding the regimen? TPT - Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy

options.label: A
options.text: There is more compliance in 3HP than 9H and 6H

options.label: C
options.text: Chance of abortion in 3 HP is same as 6H

options.label: D
options.text: 3HP regimen is less effective than 6H and 9H in preventing active TB

questions.answerText: There is more compliance in 3HP than 9H and 6H
questions.solutionHtml:
There is more compliance in 3HP than 9H and 6H
  • 3HP is a short-course TPT regimen that combines two antibiotics active against TB, INH and RPT.
  • 3HP is taken once a week for 12 weeks (12 doses in 3 months).
  • It has proven effective and safe for PLHIV and their household contacts >2 years old. Hence, option A is correct.

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with hypertriglyceridemia was started on a medication, following which, he developed flushing, hyperglycemia, and elevated liver enzymes. Identify the drug consumed by the patient:
questions.solutionHtml:
Nicotinamide
  • Nicotinic acid(Niacin) is a cutaneous vasodilator: marked flushing, heat and itching (especially in the blush area) occur after every dose. Hence, option A is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 688-689

questions.stem: A Female suffered a head injury from a road traffic accident. On examination, there is elevated intracranial pressure. Which diuretic among the following can be used in her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mannitol
  • Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic, indicated to treat increased intracranial or intraocular tension (acute congestive glaucoma, head injury, stroke, etc.): by osmotic action it encourages movement of water from brain parenchyma, CSF and aqueous humour.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 638

questions.stem: A hypertensive patient is started on a drug to control his BP. He had complaints of dry mouth, drowsiness, and confusion after taking this drug, but he still continued to take the drug for 1 year. He had to travel abroad for work, and he forgot to take his medications. He now presents with a blood pressure of 200/120mmHg. Identify the drug he was on?
questions.solutionHtml:
Clonidine
  • These are the specific side effects of the drug clonidine.
  • As clonidine causes Sedation, mental depression, disturbed sleep, dryness of mouth, nose and eyes (secretion is decreased by central action), constipation (antisecretory effect on the intestines).If we suddenly stops clonidine, it can cause rebound hypertension, so patients bp rises to 200/120 mmHg. Hence, option C is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 611-612

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs when added with erythromycin can lead to torsades de pointes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Astemizole
  • Astemizole is banned for the reason that several deaths due to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (Torsades de pointes) occurring with its higher doses or when it was coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors (erythromycin, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, etc.).


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 181

questions.stemHtml: A 2-year-old child presents to the emergency department with lethargy, difficulty feeding, and dehydration. His vitals are stable and his ECG is shown below. What is the next step in his management?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenosine 0.1 mg/kg
  • Administered by rapid i.v. injection (over 1–3 sec) either as the free base (6–12 mg) or as ATP (10–20 mg), it terminates within 30 sec. more than 90% episodes of PSVT involving the A-V node.
  • Adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV/IO first dose; maximum dose, 6 mg.
  • An ECG of a patient with PSVT will show a fast heart rate (150–250 beats per minute), a regular rhythm, and a narrow QRS complex.
  • The P wave is usually hidden within the QRS complex.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 581-582

questions.stem: An HIV patient developed a fever and dry cough. He was diagnosed with TB. He is currently on Lamivudine, Zidovudine and Nevirapine. Which Anti -TB drug should be changed in this patient?TB-Tuberculosis
questions.solutionHtml:
Rifampicin
  • Rifampin is a microsomal enzyme inducer—increases several CYP450 isoenzymes, including CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP1A2 and CYP2C subfamily.
  • It thus enhances its own metabolism as well as that of many drugs including warfarin, oral contraceptives, corticosteroids, sulfonylureas, HIV protease inhibitors, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), theophylline, metoprolol, fluconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, phenytoin, etc. Hence, it should be changed in this patient.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 818

questions.stem: A child was started on ciclesonide inhalation therapy for bronchial asthma. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding his treatment?

options.label: A
options.text: It has Fewer side effects compared to other inhalational steroids

options.label: B
options.text: It is a prodrug metabolised by bronchial esterase

options.label: C
options.text: The Occurrence of oral candidiasis is more compared to other inhaled steroids

questions.answerText: The Occurrence of oral candidiasis is more compared to other inhaled steroids
questions.solutionHtml:
The Occurrence of oral candidiasis is more compared to other inhaled steroids
  • Ciclesonide is an inhalational steroid , it is a prodrug so it will get activates inside the bronchus by enzyme bronchial esterase, hence occurence of oral candidiasis is least.
  • It has a lower oral bioavailability, and is subject to greater first-pass hepatic metabolism; this results in reduced systemic absorption from the fraction of the inhaled drug that is swallowed and thus reduced adverse effect.
  • Least-systemic effects of all ICSs; may be effective once daily.
  • Hence option C is incorrect.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 745

questions.stem: Which of the following reasons best explains the combination of Atropine (0.025 mg) and Diphenoxylate (2.5 mg) for treating secretory diarrhoea?

options.label: A
options.text: Atropine potentiates the action of smooth muscle relaxation

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents overdose and abuse of Diphenoxylate

options.label: C
options.text: It antagonizes the side effect of Diphenoxylate

options.label: D
options.text: Atropine increases the antimotility action of diphenoxylate

questions.answerText: It prevents overdose and abuse of Diphenoxylate
questions.solutionHtml:
It prevents overdose and abuse of Diphenoxylate
  • Diphenoxylate is a synthetic opioid, used exclusively as constipating agent, but because it is absorbed systemically and crosses the blood-brain barrier—CNS effects do occur i.e abuse potential.
  • Atropine is added in subpharmacological dose to discourage abuse by taking several tablets. Abuse liability is rated low, and overdose will produce disturbing atropinic side effects. Hence, option B is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 733

questions.stem: The drug 'X' is a GHRH analogue that is FDA-approved for the treatment of HIV-associated lipodystrophy and not used for Growth hormone deficiency. Identify the drug 'X':GHRH- Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone
questions.solutionHtml:
Tesamorelin
  • Tesamorelin is FDA-approved for treatment of HIV-associated lipodystrophy but not for GH deficiency.


Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 778

questions.stem: A patient with a gynecological malignancy is started on Methotrexate. Later she developed oral and gastric ulcers. Which nucleotide synthesis is affected in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
TMP
  • Methotrexate acts by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase (DHFRase), thus blocking the conversion of dihydrofolic acid (DHFA) to tetrahydrofolic acid (THFA), which leads to deficiency of TMP. Hence, option C is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page No. 921

questions.stem: In which phase of clinical trials is drug dosing done?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phase I
  • Phase I of clinical trial is related to dosing of drug. Hence, option A is correct.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition Page No. 84-85
